chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sahl, from Idrees ibn Zayd and Ali ibn Idrees, who said:

We asked Al-Reza (peace be upon him) about a man who vowed a vow that if he was freed from prison, he would fast the day in which he was freed. Then he became unable to fast due to an illness that afflicted him or for some other reason, so it prolonged for the man during his lifetime, and a lot of fasts had gathered upon him. What is the expiation of that fast? He (peace be upon him) said: 'He expiates for each day with a Mudd of wheat or barley.'

key_terms.مُدّ: Mudd (a specific volume measure of food)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a vowed fast that was missed due to illness and accumulated over time?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him), the specific legal mechanism for redeeming a perpetual vow of fasting is clarified, establishing that the expiation (kaffarah) for each missed day is the provision of a Mudd of wheat or barley. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that when a specific act of worship becomes permanently unfeasible due to chronic illness or age, it is commuted to a material charity, ensuring the vow is fulfilled without undue hardship. The specification of wheat or barley reflects the staple food standards of the time, emphasizing the practical accessibility of the redemption process for the common believer.
